content.text: {"primary_meaning":"Moral and spiritual evil—especially sin, unbelief, ignorance of God, and alienation from God—contrasted with God, truth, holiness, and salvation as “light.”","primary_basis":["John 3:19–21: people love darkness rather than light because their deeds are evil.","John 8:12 and 12:35–46: following Christ delivers people from darkness and enables them to walk in the light.","Ephesians 5:8–14: believers were formerly darkness but are now light in the Lord; darkness is associated with unfruitful works.","1 John 1:5–7 and 2:8–11: darkness is incompatible with fellowship with God and is associated with sin and hatred.","Colossians 1:13: salvation is described as rescue from the dominion of darkness.","Acts 26:18 and 1 Peter 2:9: conversion is movement from darkness to light and from Satan’s power to God.","Isaiah 9:2, applied to Jesus in Matthew 4:16: people in darkness receive the saving light of the Messiah."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Divine judgment, disaster, or eschatological exclusion rather than moral evil itself.","basis":["Exodus 10:21–23: darkness is a plague of judgment upon Egypt.","Amos 5:18–20 and Joel 2:1–2, 31: the Day of the Lord is characterized by darkness.","Matthew 8:12; 22:13; 25:30: “outer darkness” signifies exclusion and punishment.","Mark 13:24 and Revelation 16:10: cosmic or supernatural darkness accompanies judgment."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Suffering, grief, oppression, or adverse circumstances.","basis":["Job 19:8 and 30:26: darkness expresses affliction and disappointed hope.","Psalm 88:6, 12, 18: darkness represents profound suffering, abandonment, and despair.","Isaiah 9:2 and 58:10: darkness describes distress or oppression from which deliverance comes.","Lamentations 3:2: affliction is portrayed as being driven into darkness without light."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Death, the grave, or the realm of the dead.","basis":["Job 10:21–22: death’s destination is described as a land of darkness.","Psalm 88:10–12: darkness and forgetfulness are associated with the grave.","Psalm 107:10, 14: “darkness and the shadow of death” depict mortal peril and captivity."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Divine hiddenness, mystery, or the concealed presence of God; here darkness is not evil.","basis":["Exodus 20:21: Moses approaches the thick darkness where God is.","1 Kings 8:12 and 2 Chronicles 6:1: God is said to dwell in thick darkness.","Psalm 18:11: God makes darkness his covering."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Primordial unformedness or the absence of created illumination and order.","basis":["Genesis 1:2–5: darkness covers the deep before light is called forth and distinguished from darkness.","This reading is especially prominent in creation studies, where the darkness need not itself represent moral evil."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Secrecy, concealment, or lack of disclosure without necessarily implying moral evil.","basis":["Psalm 139:11–12: darkness can conceal from humans but not from God.","Matthew 10:27 and Luke 12:3: what is spoken or hidden in darkness is contrasted with public disclosure."],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is a settled dominant Christian symbolic association between darkness and the complex of evil, sin, unbelief, spiritual ignorance, and alienation from God. It is not an exclusive meaning: biblical usage is strongly context-dependent, and darkness can also signify judgment, suffering, death, concealment, primordial conditions, or even God’s hidden presence."}
